articles.summary:

articles.title: Hong Kong leader calls for stronger construction oversight amid One Stanley case
articles.summary:
Hong Kong will strengthen its regulatory regime and impose stiffer penalties to ensure strong deterrence against building violations, the city leader has pledged, following a series of substandard construction scandals including the latest controversy involving a luxury residential development in Stanley.

Chinese actress Li Bingbing credits success to younger sister who acts as manager, confidante

From a humble working-class family in northeast China to becoming a celebrated actress on the Hollywood stage, 53-year-old Li Bingbing’s ascent has never been a solo journey.
At the heart of her decades-long career is her younger sister, Li Xue, 51, who transitioned from journalism to become Li Bingbing’s manager. Together, they co-founded Hesong Entertainment, a talent company that has represented performers across generations.

articles.title: Beijing’s policy advisers map out how post-reunification Taiwan could be governed
articles.summary:
In 2019, President Xi Jinping became the first Chinese leader to publicly call for the exploration of detailed proposals for governing Taiwan after reunification.
Seven years later, the first proposals from a handful of the mainland’s leading research institutes have either been finalised or are nearing completion, the South China Morning Post has learned.

articles.title: Hong Kong’s bridge of gold completes China’s yuan ambition
articles.summary:
Beijing’s push to accumulate gold serves a larger goal: yuan internationalisation. In this series, Part I traces China’s path to becoming a gold superpower, while this article explores Hong Kong’s key role in safeguarding the nation’s financial security.

articles.title: Hong Kong temperatures drop to 23 degrees Celsius on Tuesday morning, lowest this autumn
articles.summary:
Temperatures in Hong Kong dropped to about 23 degrees Celsius (73 Fahrenheit) on Tuesday morning, the lowest so far this autumn.
According to the Hong Kong Observatory, the cooler weather was caused by a dry northeast monsoon.
“A dry northeast monsoon will bring mainly fine weather to the coast of Guangdong in the next couple of days. It will be windier and slightly cooler in the morning over the region,” the forecaster said.

articles.title: Experts urge wider One Stanley checks, tighter paperwork after steel bar shortfall
articles.summary:
Hong Kong’s building authorities should consider inspecting the remaining properties in a luxury residential development and tightening work process documentation after one house was found to have used insufficient steel bars during construction, experts have said.

articles.title: Marine’s arrest for murder in Japan fuels anger over US military presence
articles.summary:
The alleged murder of an Okinawan woman by a US marine has put newly elected Governor Genta Koja under intense pressure, raising questions about whether the incident could deepen opposition against the American military presence just as Okinawa assumes greater importance in Japan’s regional security strategy.

articles.title: How a Hong Kong property investor still made US$30 million – after a 40% price cut
articles.summary:
Amid concerns over rising interest rates and a weak retail property market, a long-time investor has sold a portfolio of prime street shops in Tsim Sha Tsui – held for more than four decades – and locked in a profit of nearly HK$237 million (US$30.2 million) despite accepting a deal more than 40 per cent below his original asking price.

articles.title: US seeks to revoke citizenship of 2 China-born men convicted in Beijing-linked cases
articles.summary:
The US Justice Department (DOJ) is seeking to revoke the citizenship of a former Navy sailor convicted of spying for China and a Florida man convicted of conspiring to act as an agent of Beijing, it announced on Monday.
Jinchao Wei and Ping Li are among 40 people facing denaturalisation actions in what the department described as the largest batch of such filings under the Trump administration. The civil proceedings remain pending, with no determination of liability, the DOJ said.

articles.title: US accuses mainland China of targeting Taiwan leader’s family in surveillance case
articles.summary:
The United States has accused mainland China of hiring an American citizen of Chinese origin to surveil the family of Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te, days after President Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation on Sunday arrested 34-year-old Zhang Wanying at Los Angeles International Airport, alleging that she attempted to flee the country and charged her with acting as an unregistered agent for the Chinese government.

articles.title: Trump says US moved bombers from UK airbase after threats
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that a threat linked to Iran ⁠had prompted the removal of American B-1 bombers from a British airbase.
The planes had been stationed at RAF Fairford, the preferred European base for US bombers, and had recently been used in US strikes on Iran. Last week, five British men were arrested near the base – which Iran’s Revolutionary Guards previously said was a legitimate target – on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts.

articles.title: Hong Kong must scrap housing plan and preserve golf course
articles.summary:
The hotly contested court battle over government plans to build 12,000 public flats on Hong Kong’s oldest golf course has played its final round. The government decided not to appeal against a ruling that held its approval of an environmental impact assessment (EIA) report on the project to be unlawful.
This is better than pursuing a further attempt to persuade the courts to uphold a fatally flawed process. Now, a broader review of the plans can be undertaken in light of the Court of Appeal’s...

articles.title: Mainland Chinese favour diplomacy to achieve Taiwan reunification with caveats: survey
articles.summary:
Mainland Chinese prefer coercion over military force to settle the “reunification question” with Taiwan, and their opinion of the US remains low, although they favour engaging with Washington on trade and security.
These are the results from the latest survey of mainland citizens, conducted between April 16 and June 26. This straddled the first summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing but came before the second one in Washington last month.

articles.title: Beijing wanted more from Xi’s state visit to Washington
articles.summary:
Xi Jinping’s state visit to Washington in September was steeped in pageantry. The Chinese president received two 21-gun salutes in three days, watched a flyover by the powerful B-2 stealth bomber, and viewed the founding documents of American democracy at the National Archives.

articles.title: Russia plays down plague reports after lab worker death
articles.summary:
Russia on Monday sought to play down reports that a laboratory technician had died of plague, even as US President Donald Trump said Washington was closely monitoring the situation and offered US help.
Reports on Friday that pneumonic plague had killed a 28-year-old woman named Darya Shipilova, who had been working for the anti-plague institute in Siberia’s Irkutsk region, sparked alarm.

articles.title: US search for missing airmen in China gains new attention after Xi-Trump summit
articles.summary:
For more than eight decades, the remains of US fighter pilot Morton Sher lay unrecovered in China. A photograph of a memorial to him in a Hunan village eventually helped investigators find where his plane crashed in 1943.
Sher was buried in his hometown of Greenville, South Carolina, in December 2025, a homecoming that offers a rare example of what US-China cooperation can achieve for families of missing servicemen.

articles.title: Bid to turn 14 subsidised Hong Kong sale flats into subdivided homes raises abuse concerns
articles.summary:
The owners of 14 subsidised sale flats have applied for a grace period to comply with Hong Kong’s new regulatory regime for subdivided homes, the housing minister has revealed, raising concerns that public resources were being abused.
The cases were disclosed on Monday at a Legislative Council housing panel meeting when lawmaker Mark Chong Ho-fung asked Secretary for Housing Winnie Ho Wing-yin about the use of subsidised sale flats as subdivided units for renting.

articles.title: France, Germany call for new weapon allowing ‘immediate cut off’ of China from EU market
articles.summary:
In the strongest sign yet of a shifting European Union policy on China, the leaders of France and Germany have demanded a new trade weapon that would cut off access to the EU market when third countries cause severe distortions.

archive.security_status_cs: Geopolitické napětí v Indo-Pacifiku přetrvává, podpořené dodávkami stíhaček F-16V na Tchaj-wan a rostoucími obavami v Malajsii ohledně situace v Jihočínském moři. Ekonomický vývoj v regionu je smíšený: zatímco Hongkong hlásí oživení maloobchodních tržeb během svátků, IPO trh nadále oslabuje a technologické restrikce (např. blokování VPN pro AI modely) se zostřují.

Regional economic dynamics are mixed: while Hong Kong reports retail growth during holidays, its IPO market struggles and tech restrictions (such as VPN blocks for AI models) tighten.

archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostření debat ohledně nových evropských nástrojů na ochranu obchodu před čínskými distorzemi a další diplomatické manévry kolem USA a Tchaj-wanu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, intensified debates regarding new European trade defense tools against Chinese distortions and further diplomatic maneuvers surrounding the US and Taiwan are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Geopolitické napětí v Indo-Pacifiku nadále roste v důsledku posilování vojenské spolupráce USA (včetně prvního nasazení stíhaček F-35 v Indii) a rostoucích obav ohledně Tchaj-wanu a špionážních aktivit. Evropská unie zároveň přitvrzuje vůči čínskému obchodu skrze nové návrhy na tržní bariéry, zatímco Hongkong čelí vnitřním ekonomickým a regulatorním výzvám.
archive.security_status_en: Geopolitical tensions in the Indo-Pacific remain elevated due to deepened US military cooperation—marked by the first deployment of F-35 jets in India—and mounting concerns over Taiwan and espionage activities. Simultaneously, the European Union is hardening its stance on Chinese trade through proposed market barriers, while Hong Kong grapples with internal economic and regulatory challenges.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další diplomatické manévry kolem obchodních vztahů mezi EU a Čínou a zvýšenou ostražitost v oblasti regionální bezpečnosti v Asii.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic maneuvering regarding EU-China trade relations and heightened vigilance concerning regional security in Asia are expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Geopolitické napětí v Asii a Tichomoří nadále roste v důsledku prohlubující se americko-čínské konfrontace, včetně obvinění ze špionáže a sledování rodiny tchaj-wanští představitelů. Současně Francie a Německo tlačí na EU, aby zavedla tvrdé obchodní restrikce vůči Číně, což zvyšuje riziko globální obchodní fragmentace.
archive.security_status_en: Geopolitical tensions in the Asia-Pacific remain elevated due to deepening US-China friction, including espionage charges and surveillance targeting the family of Taiwan's leader. Simultaneously, France and Germany are pushing the EU to adopt aggressive trade restrictions against China, heightening the risk of global trade fragmentation.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřenou rétoriku mezi Bruselem a Pekingem ohledně nových obchodních nástrojů EU a pokračující sledování bezpečnostní situace kolem Tchaj-wanu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened rhetoric between Brussels and Beijing regarding new EU trade tools and continued monitoring of the security situation around Taiwan are expected.
